question: Consider the pytest test `werkzeug_qa/serving_readinto_s3_state/files/testcase.py::TestDechunkedReadinto::test_readinto_varied_buffers` (test file `werkzeug_qa/serving_readinto_s3_state/files/testcase.py`, class `TestDechunkedReadinto`, single test method `test_readinto_varied_buffers`). During this test the method `werkzeug.serving.DechunkedInput.readinto` defined in `src/werkzeug/serving.py` is called many times. An invocation is one call of that method during the test run; invocations are numbered 1, 2, 3, ... in chronological order of their calls. Consider invocation number 7. In the body of `readinto`, the local variable `read` is assigned by exactly three statements: `read = 0`, `read = len(buf)`, and `read += n` (the augmented assignment counts as an assignment). Report the full ordered history of `read` within invocation 7: one entry per execution of any of those three assignment statements in that invocation, in the chronological order in which they executed, where the entry's value is the value `read` holds immediately after that statement has finished executing. Every execution produces an entry, even if the value equals the previous one (no deduplication); the initial `read = 0` is the first entry. `step` is the 1-based position of the entry in this history (an integer). `value` is the Python `repr()` of the integer value given as a JSON string (e.g. the integer seven is written as "7", not 7). Answer with `{"value_history": [{"step": <int>, "value": <repr string>}, ...]}`, sorted by `step` ascending.
